newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa studies petrochemical projects - Erwin.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa studies petrochemical projects - Erwin.

text.p: South Africa is negotiating petrochemical projects with a number of possible partners, but a proposed Taiwanese plant has been ruled out, Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin said on Thursday.
Erwin told a parliamentary news briefing that Taiwan itself had indicated it was no longer interested in the project in South Africa.

"This was a proposal made by them ... there were some aspects we thought were not feasible and did not meet our specific needs... in its form as presented by the Taiwanese, we would not implement that for a range of technical reasons," he said.

"We however are independently continuing the exploration of the petrochemical downstream, we have opened negotiations with a number of other partners, which still include the Taiwanese if they wish to come in.
"This would be one of the key targetted projects that we'll be examining this year," Erwin added.
